item.title: EXPERIMENT OVER. Yesterday i got banned from LinkedIn. this is my formal…
item.description:
EXPERIMENT OVER. Yesterday i got banned from LinkedIn.
this is my formal apology-after-being-canceled post.
which is funny, because for the last 3 months people have been asking me:
“why do you post such eye bleach things?” “why do you change your bio every single day?” “does your day job pay you to do this?”
simply, i was trying to break through the noise and make people laugh while doing it.
i run the branded social accounts for Clay, which means i spend all day thinking about how companies, creators, and execs should talk online.
the thing is, if you know me, i do not like talking like a professional. i do not have it in me.
this might handicap my corporate career, but truly, i do not want to be someone i'm not.
during my time in J-school and writing newsletters for 6AM City, and growing up reading Morning Brew, i learned to write/talk as if i was talking to a friend on the couch.
through watching wrastling, i learned to turn the dial 10% of who my “voice” is. and through making LinkedIn my living, i studied the actual shapes of micro-blog-style posts.
together, this is my "sauce" and it can't be replicated.
and somehow, what started as a dumb competition with Owen Ciha to just rip more daily personal posts, mixed with jealousy over Sarah Khasrovi’s viral one-liners, mixed with watching Alex Lieberman turn an audience into power, brand deals, and distribuush, turned into 3,000 new followers in 3 months.
i changed my bio every day to match my weird posts and treated LinkedIn like a little lab for whatever was wrong with my brain that morning.
then yesterday i flew too close to the sun.
perhaps I used to many "💦" emojis.
but when my personal account got temporarily banned, it also put the brand accounts i run in a weird spot, because you need a personal account to manage company pages -- I nearly pooped myself.
SOOO. it’s safe to say the experiment worked, but idk if i’m returning to “the life” for a while. at least not in the current way.
truly became the most eye bleach account on here imo.
until next time.
✌️
(thanks LinkedIn for helping me)

item.title: Are we in agreement? If we’re in agreement, then I think we’re aligned. And if we’re…
item.description:
Are we in agreement?
If we’re in agreement, then I think we’re aligned.
And if we’re aligned, it’s safe to say we’re completely on the same page.
Because when we’re on the same page, we are truly operating in lockstep.
Operating in lockstep naturally means our synergies are fully optimized across the board.
And when our synergies are optimized, we are effectively moving the needle in a meaningful way.
If the needle is moving, then we’re clearly tracking seamlessly toward our mission-critical KPIs.
Tracking toward our KPIs requires us to touch base, circle back, and ensure we have the necessary bandwidth.
I'll put time on the cal to circle back.
Because if we circle back with enough bandwidth, we can safely take things offline to look under the hood.
Taking it offline ensures we can boil the ocean without leaving any money on the table.
And if there’s absolutely no money left on the table, we’ve successfully engineered a definitive win-win scenario.
A win-win scenario means we’ve reached a holistic, cross-functional strategic consensus.
And if we have a strategic consensus...
Then I think we’re in agreement.
If not, then let's blow bubbles on it.
Thoughts?

item.title: this line made me 9 figures by 25: HR called me into a room with my manager. my boss:…
item.description:
this line made me 9 figures by 25:
HR called me into a room with my manager.
my boss: “you’re fired” me: “i know you are but what am i”
and that’s how i fired my boss + took all her assets. the room went silent.
so i slid across the conference table on my stomach like a penguin in gucci loafers.
made every light red.
took out my blade.
peeled bark off the ficus in the corner.
extracted the syrup.
turned it into glue.
sealed the door shut.
karate chopped my boss in the dick.
yeah you read that right.
roundhouse kicked HR, too.
security was coming. legal was coming. Jared from Subway somehow took a finance job here, and now he was coming too. that scared me most.
so i opened the window.
we were 100 stories high.
i broke into the janator closet, found 4 plunger suction cups, and tied them to my hands + feet with SaaStr Ai lanyards.
then i scaled the building.
halfway up, i remembered i had fired my boss, which technically made me acting CEO. so i ordered the company helicopter.
the helicopter took me to my boss’s island manor.
i karate chopped the pilot in the dick and parachuted out.
ripped the cord 4 feet above the ground. Caitlin Clark was mid-jump shot on the island court.
i stuffed it. clean block. all ball. took the ball, bounced it off every security guard’s head, then spun it on my finger while logging into Workday.
first thing i did as CEO: approve my own PTO. then I transfer all the money into my Liberty Bank Mutual Savings Account (#partner)
then my boss came outside in a linen robe holding room-temperature milk.
she said, “you’ll never get away with this.”
i said, “circle back.”
i threw the glass of milk into the ocean.
a dolphin came up wearing a Bain vest. i promoted him to chief of staff.
he opened a Notion doc, and titled it “Q3 takeover plan.”
i said, “make it lower cog.”
he nodded because he understood leadership.
then the board arrived by jet ski. 11 men named Tom.
they asked me for the numbers. so i showed them the damn numbers. they started clapping. I karate chopped them all in the dick.
Jared from finance started crying.
Caitlin Clark asked if i wanted to run a pick and roll.
i said, “i’m more of an operator.”
then i walked into the manor.
there was a vault behind a painting of my boss shaking hands with Monopoly man. i opened it with Face ID because, again, i was acting CEO.
inside was:
- $400 million - 3 Dell monitors - a signed photo of Mark Cuban - a tiny hotel bible - my original offer letter - a sticky note that said “do not let brad near the ficus”
that’s when it hit me.
success comes down to credentials, permission, drive, hunger, determination, and extracting glue from office plants under pressure. anyone can do this.
you just need to believe in yourself.
comment "TIME WASTE" for the playbook.
